'''Władysław Roman Orlicz''' ({{small|Polish:}} {{IPAc-pl|w|ł|a|'|d|y|s|ł|a|f|-|'|o|r|l|i|cz}}; May 24, 1903 – August 9, 1990) was a Polish [[mathematician]] linked to the circle of the [[Lwów School of Mathematics]]. He was a professor at the [[University of Poznań]] and a member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. From 1977 to 1979, he served as president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].

He is known for his research in [[functional analysis]], [[topology]], [[vector-valued function]]s, [[orthogonality (mathematics)|orthogonal series]] and [[measure theory]]. Concepts named after him include [[Orlicz space]]s and the [[Orlicz–Pettis theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maligranda |first=Lech |last2=Wnuk |first2=Witold |date=2004 |title=Władysław Orlicz (1903-1990). A biography |url=https://eudml.org/doc/282016 |journal=Banach Center Publications |volume=64 |issue=1 |pages=13–19 |issn=0137-6934}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Orlicz was born on 24 May 1903 in [[Okocim]], then part of the [[Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria]] within [[Austria-Hungary]], as the third out of five children of Franciszek Orlicz and Maria ({{nee|Rossknecht}}).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/edit/10.1201/9781482270501-6/wtadyslaw-orlicz-life-contributions-mathematics-lech-maligranda-witold-wnuk |title=Wtadyslaw Orlicz: His Life and Contributions to Mathematics |website=taylorfrancis.com |author=Witold Wnuk, Lech Maligranda |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> His father died when he was four years old. Orlicz attended schools in [[Tarnów]], [[Znojmo]] (now in [[Czech Republic]]), and [[Lwów]] (now in [[Ukraine]]), where his family settled in 1919. As a student, Orlicz excelled especially in the upper grades. He graduated in 1920 from the State Second Real School in Lwów ([[Polish language|Polish]]: ''Państwowa Druga Szkoła Realna we Lwowie'') and voluntarily enlisted in the [[Polish Armed Forces|Polish Army]],  although he did not take part in any fighting during the [[Polish-Soviet War]] (1919–2021).<ref name="UAM">{{cite web|url=https://wmi.amu.edu.pl/zycie-naukowe/cykle-wykladow/wyklady-im.-wladyslawa-orlicza/biografia-prof.-wladyslawa-orlicza |language=pl |title=Biografia prof. Władysława Orlicza |trans-title=Biography of Professor Władysław Orlicz |work=Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, Adam Mickiewicz University |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref>

Orlicz initially enrolled at the [[Lwów Polytechnic]] but after a year he changed the university and began studying in the Department of Mathematical and Natural Sciences of the [[Jan Kazimierz University]] (now the [[University of Lviv]]). His professors included [[Stefan Banach]], [[Hugo Steinhaus]] and [[Antoni Łomnicki]].<ref name="Maligranda">{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Orlicz/ |title=Władysław Orlicz |author=Lech Maligranda |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive  |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> In 1923, still as a student, he started working at the university, first as a demonstrator, and later as a research assistant. In 1925, Orlicz finished his studies at the university but he continued his education attending [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]]'s lectures at the [[Lviv University of Technology|Lwów Polytechnic]].<ref name="Maligranda" />

In 1926, at the age of 23, he published his first paper on the theory of summability, which was published in the ''[[Tohoku Mathematical Journal]]''.<ref name="UAM" /> In 1928, Orlicz earned his doctorate under [[Eustachy Żyliński]], based on his dissertation entitled ''Z teorii szeregów ortogonalnych'' (On the  Theory of Orthogonal Series).<ref name="Matysiak">{{cite web|url=https://www.archpan.poznan.pl/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Materialy-Wladyslawa-Orlicza-1903-1990-sygn.-P.-III-91.pdf |language=pl |title=Materiały Władysława Orlicza (1903-1990) |trans-title=The Władysław Orlicz Papers (1903-1990) |work=Polish Academy of Sciences |author=Jarosław Matysiak |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> Orlicz influenced the young mathematician [[Józef Marcinkiewicz]] through their collaboration on this subject in the mid-1930s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://norbertwiener.umd.edu/NW/Marcinkiewicz_Bio_2.pdf |title=Józef Marcinkiewicz–his life and work |work=norbertwiener.umd.edu |author=Roman Sznajder |page=4 |date=19 March 2019 |access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> He was known to visit the [[Scottish Café]] and engage in mathematical discussions with many prominent mathematicians of the time. He was the author or co-author of 14 problems included in the ''[[Scottish Book]]''.<ref name="Maligranda" />

In 1927–1929 and 1930–1931, Orlicz was employed as a teacher in a military cadet school and a private high school for girls.<ref name="UAM" /> From 1929 to 1930, Orlicz pursued further studies in [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Göttingen]]<ref name="Maligranda" /> after having received a scholarship from the Ministry of Religious Affairs and Public Education. His teachers included [[Max Born]], [[Richard Courant]], [[Edmund Landau]], and [[Harald Bohr]].<ref name="UAM" /> During his stay in [[Göttingen]], Orlicz began working with [[Zygmunt Birnbaum]] on the subject of the extension of spaces. This led to Orlicz's subsequent independent research on [[function space]]s that generalize [[lp space|''L''<sup>p</sup> spaces]], now known as [[Orlicz space]]s.<ref name="Maligranda" /><ref name="UAM" />

Upon his return to Lwów in 1930, Orlicz received the position of senior assistant in the Faculty of Mathematics of the Lwów Polytechnic. In 1934, he obtained his [[habilitation]] on the basis of his work in the field of [[Orthogonality (mathematics)|orthogonal series]] and the following year, he was promoted to the position of [[assistant professor]] at the Lwów Polytechnic.<ref name="Murawski">{{cite web|url=https://wmi.amu.edu.pl/en/faculty/history/biographical-sketches/wladyslaw-orlicz |title=Władysław Orlicz |author=Roman Murawski |work=Adam Mickiewicz University |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> In 1937, he became an extraordinary professor at the [[University of Poznań]] following a nomination from President [[Ignacy Mościcki]].<ref name="UAM" />
[[Image:27 Prospekt Shevchenka, Lviv.jpg|thumb|240px|Building that used to house the original [[Scottish Café]], now in [[Lviv]], Ukraine]]
The outbreak of the [[World War II]] surprised him while he was on vacation in Lwów. Since he could not return to Poznań, he was appointed professor and continued to lecture at the Faculty of Mathematics of the University of Lwów until June 1941. During the [[Occupation of Poland (1939–1945)|Nazi occupation]] of Lwów (1941–1944), he worked at Professor [[Rudolf Weigl]]'s Typhus Research Institute as a [[louse-feeder|lice feeder]], alongside [[Stefan Banach]]. This allowed him to avoid German repression and to support himself financially.<ref name="UAM" />

When the war ended, Orlicz could not remain in Lwów as the [[Polish population transfers in 1944–1946|forced resettlement of Poles from the Eastern Borderlands]] took place. He returned to Poznań, taking over the Chair of Mathematics at the University of Poznań (now [[Adam Mickiewicz University]]). In 1948, Orlicz was awarded the title of ordinary professor.

In 1956, Orlicz became a corresponding member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]], advancing to full membership in 1961.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://poznan.pan.pl/obiekt/prof-dr-hab-wladyslaw-orlicz/ |language=pl |title=Prof. rd hab. Władysław Orlicz |work=Polish Academy of Sciences |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> Orlicz worked at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] until 1974 when he retired.<ref name="Maligranda" />

Orlicz was as an editor of ''Commentationes Mathematicae'' (1955–1990), and ''[[Studia Mathematica]]'' (1962–1990). He served as President of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] from 1977 to 1979.<ref name="Maligranda" /> He was also a member of the [[Warsaw Scientific Society]] and the [[Polish Philosophical Society]].<ref name="UAM" />

On 23 August 1980, he was among the signatories of the Appeal of the Sixty-Four, joining prominent writers, public intellectuals, and scholars in their effort to persuade the [[Communism in Poland|communist authorities]] to engage in dialogue with the [[History of Solidarity#Early strikes (1980)|protesting workers]].<ref name="UAM" /> He continued to host a seminar "Selected Problems of Functional Analysis" at the University of Poznań until 1989. His doctoral students included [[Andrzej Alexiewicz]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wmi.amu.edu.pl/wydzial/historia/biogramy/andrzej-alexiewicz |language=pl |title=Andrzej Alexiewicz |website=Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, Adam Mickiewicz University |author=Roman Murawski |access-date=25 July 2026}}</ref> [[Feliks Barański]],<ref name="MathGen">{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=51907&utm_source=copilot.com |title=Władysław Roman Orlicz |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=25 July 2026}}</ref> [[Zbigniew Ciesielski]],<ref name="MathGen" /> and [[Stanisław Knapowski]].<ref name="MathGen" /> He died on 9 August 1990 in Poznań.<ref name="Maligranda" />

==Work==
Orlicz made significant contributions to such areas of mathematics as [[function space]]s, [[orthogonality (mathematics)|orthogonal series]], unconditional convergence in [[Banach space]]s, summability, [[vector-valued function]]s, metric locally convex spaces, [[real function]]s, [[measure theory]] and integration, polynomial operators and modular spaces.

One of Orlicz's most well-known contributions to mathematics is the introduction of [[Orlicz space]]s, a type of [[function space]]s which generalizes [[lp space|''L''<sup>p</sup> spaces]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.problemsolving.fi/pp/orliczBook2.pdf |title=Orlicz spaces and Generalized Orlicz spaces |author=Petteri Harjulehto, Peter Hästö |date=20 February 2019 |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> They were first formulated in his 1932 paper entitled ''Über eine gewisse Klasse von Räumen vom Typus B'' and published in ''Bulletin International de l’Académie Polonaise des Sciences''.<ref>[https://www.fuw.edu.pl/~kostecki/scans/orlicz1932.pdf Über eine gewisse Klasse von Räumen vom Typus B], Bull. Internat. Acad. Polon. Sci. Lett., Class. Sci. Math. Natur.: Sér. A, Sci. Math. 1932:8/9, 207–220.</ref> [[Stefan Banach]] himself had already acknowledged in his monograph published the same year that Orlicz was the first one who introduced those spaces.<ref>Stefan Banach, 1932, Théorie des opérations linéaires, Warszawa (p.202)</ref> Orlicz spaces have found wide application in  [[mathematical analysis|analysis]], [[integral equation]]s, [[probability]], [[constructive function theory]], [[differential equation]]s, and [[mathematical statistics]].<ref name="Maligranda" />

The [[Orlicz-Pettis theorem]] is a result in [[functional analysis]] relating to [[convergent series]] or, equivalently, [[countable additivity]] of [[measure (mathematics)|measures]] with values in abstract spaces.<ref>W. Orlicz, [http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/sm/sm1/sm1114.pdf Beiträge zur Theorie der Orthogonalentwicklungen II], ''[[Studia Mathematica]]'' '''1''' (1929),  241–255.</ref><ref>W. Filter and I. Labuda,  [https://math.wp.olemiss.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2018/07/filter-labuda.pdf Essays on the Orlicz-Petts theorem, I (The two theorems)], ''[[Real Analysis Exchange]]'' '''16(2)''', 1990-91, 393--403.</ref> Together with {{ill|Julian Musielak|pl|Julian Musielak}}, Orlicz introduced the concept in [[mathematical analysis]] known as [[Bounded variation#Weighted BV functions|weighted BV function]]s.

Other eponymous concepts appearing in the mathematical literature include the Orlicz property, Orlicz category theorem, [[Hahn-Banach theorem#For nonlinear functions|Mazur-Orlicz theorem]], Orlicz interpolation theorem, Musielak-Orlicz space, [[Orlicz space#Orlicz norm of a random variable|Orlicz norm]], Hardy-Orlicz spaces, Marcinkiewicz-Orlicz spaces and Orlicz-Sobolev spaces.<ref name="Maligranda" />

==Awards and recognition==
[[File:Władysław Orlicz tablica Poznań.jpg|thumb|240px|Władysław Orlicz memorial plaque in [[Poznań]]]]
During his scientific career Orlicz received a number of awards and state decorations including [[Stefan Banach Prize]] of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] (1948),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Władysław Orlicz {{!}} Polskie Towarzystwo Matematyczne |url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/laureaci/wladyslaw-orlicz |access-date=2026-07-24 |website=www.ptm.org.pl}}</ref> the [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Golden Cross of Merit]] (1954),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/mp/1954/s/112/1566 |language=pl |title=Uchwała Rady Państwa z dnia 16 lipca 1954 r. o nadaniu odznaczeń państwowych |trans-title=Resolution of the Council of State of 16 July 1954 on the Awarding of State Decorations |work=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> [[Medal of the 10th Anniversary of People's Poland]] (1955),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/mp/1955/s/112/1450 |language=pl |title=Lista osób odznaczonych „Medalem 10-lecia Polski Ludowej” |trans-title=List of Recipients of the Medal of the 10th Anniversary of the Polish People’s Republic |work=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> the Commander's Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]] (1958), Honorary Membership of the Polish Mathematical Society (1973), [[Jurzykowski Prize]] (1973),<ref name="Duda" /> Copernicus Medal of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (1973), [[Wacław Sierpiński]] Medal of the [[University of Warsaw]] (1979), Medal of the Commission for National Education (1983) and the Individual State Prizes (2nd degree in 1952,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pbc.gda.pl/Content/102766/Nr_203.pdf |language=pl |title=Uchwała Prezydium Rządu w sprawie przyznania nagród za osiągnięcia w dziedzinie nauki, postępu technicznego, literatury i sztuki za rok 1952 |trans-title=Resolution of the Presidium of the Government concerning the awarding of prizes for achievements in science, technological progress, literature, and the arts for the year 1952 |work=Trybuna Ludu |page=6 |date=23 July 1953 |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> 1st degree in 1966).<ref name="Duda">{{cite book |last=Duda |first=Roman |date=2012 |title=Matematycy XIX i XX wieku związani z Polską |trans-title=19th and 20th-Century Mathematicians Connected with Poland |language=pl |publisher=Wydawnictwo Uniwersytetu Wrocławskiego |location=Wrocław |isbn=978-83-229-3316-9 |page= |url= }}</ref>

Orlicz participated at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] on four occasions: [[Oslo]] (1936), [[Edinburgh]] (1958), [[Stockholm]] (1962) and [[Warsaw]] (1983), where he served as honorary president. He authored or co-authored 171 scientific papers and oversaw 39 doctoral dissertations. His influence on the mathematical community in Poznań was immense and he is sometimes described as the founder of the Poznań School of Mathematics.<ref name="UAM" />

He was the recipient of [[honorary doctorate]]s from [[York University]] in Canada (1974),<ref name="Maligranda" /> [[Poznań University of Technology]] (1978)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www3.put.poznan.pl/jubileusz/honoriscausa |language=pl |title=Doktorzy honoris causa Politechniki Poznańskiej |trans-title=Honorary Doctorates of the Poznan University of Technology |work=Poznan University of Technology |date=4 April 2011 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122937/http://www3.put.poznan.pl/jubileusz/honoriscausa |archive-date=2016-03-04}}</ref> and [[Adam Mickiewicz University]] (1983).

The Orlicz Memorial Conference was held in March, 1991 by the [[University of Mississippi]] in [[Oxford, Mississippi|Oxford]], United States. Other conferences in memory of Orlicz were organized in 1998 by the [[Adam Mickiewicz University]] in [[Poznań]], and in 2000 by the Adam Mickiewicz University and the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] in [[Bedlewo]].<ref name="Maligranda" />

==Personal life==
Orlicz had four brothers: Kazimierz, Tadeusz, Zbigniew and Michał. Zbigniew died in the [[Polish-Soviet War]] (1919–1921). Kazimierz, the eldest brother, perished in the [[Stutthof concentration camp]]. The remaining brothers became professors: Tadeusz specialized in timber technology while Michał in [[climatology]] and [[metereology]].<ref name="UAM" />

In 1928, Orlicz married Zofia ({{nee|Krzysik}}). She was an assistant in the Faculty of Physics at the [[Jan Kazimierz University]] in [[Lwów]]. During [[World War II]], she served in the [[Home Army]] and was awarded the Order of [[Virtuti Militari]] for her involvement in saving Jewish children from the [[Holocaust]]. After the war, she was persecuted by the communist authorities and spent five years in prison (1948–1953) for distributing banned press.<ref name="UAM" />
